sentences.text: The genus name Paraprotopteryx means "near Protopteryx" because it resembles that genus, while the specific name gracilis is intended to mean "pretty".

This bird possessed a Y-shaped furcula with a narrow angle between the clavicles, an unusually shaped breastbone that distinguished it from other enantiornitheans, and a carpometacarpus that was only partially fused.
Paraprotopteryx had four rectrices ten centimeters long that more than doubled its total body length, potentially marking an important step in feather evolution.
The tail feathers featured very elongated ribbon-like shafts with barbs and expansion only at the tips.
The species Paraprotopteryx gracilis was named and described in 2007 by Zheng Xiaoting, Zhang Zihui, and Hou Lianhai.
The holotype specimen STM V001 consists of a skeleton with a skull mounted on a plate and counterplate.
The species description relies on rump parts where preserved feathers indicate the specimen was a subadult.
Paraprotopteryx belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes and is classified under the class Reptilia.
The time range for Paraprotopteryx is the Hauterivian, from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
Researchers suggested in 2008 that the fossil correlates with beds dated to approximately 122 million years ago.
While the second pair of ribbon-like rectrices is certain, some researchers suspect it might be the result of artifice.
